fields.Name: Rhythm Software
fields.Description: Rhythm Software AMS connector — syncs contacts, organizations, memberships, committees, events, certifications, finance, commerce, fundraising, awards, accreditation, sponsorship and submissions via the Rhythm REST API (15 per-module OpenAPI specs).

Configuration.AuthNotes: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials (M2M) via Auth0. POST https://<auth0Domain>/oauth/token with grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, and audience=https://api.rhythmsoftware.com. Returns a Bearer JWT valid for 24h. M2M tokens have a monthly request budget (vendor-configured per tenant, not documented as a fixed limit in the OpenAPI specs). An alternative querystring-authorizer (access_token header) is available per Platform spec — primary flow is Bearer JWT.
Configuration.TokenRefreshNotes: No refresh token issued. Token expires in 24h (typically). Reissue by repeating the client_credentials grant. Auth0 domain is tenant-specific and provided in the credential schema.
Configuration.APIVersioningNotes: Each module URL embeds the version implicitly via the spec filename (v1). The info.version field across all 15 specs is "v1-2025-04-18". Version is encoded in the OpenAPI spec filename, not a separate header or param.
Configuration.NavigationBaseURLNotes: Rhythm exposes 15 independent per-module subdomains. There is no single base URL. Each module has its own subdomain (rolodex, membership, committees, events, certifications, careers, collect, commerce, fundraising, awards, platform, system, accreditation, sponsorship, submissions). The connector must route requests to the correct subdomain per IO.

PaginationDefaults.notes: DynamoDB-style keyset cursor pagination. All list endpoints accept ?exclusiveStartKey=<string> for subsequent pages. Response envelopes carry { Count, Items, LastEvaluatedKey } — when LastEvaluatedKey is absent or null, the final page has been reached. No page-size param documented in the specs (server-controlled page size). The search endpoints (POST .../search) also accept exclusiveStartKey as a body/query param.

IncrementalSyncCapability.notes: No list-endpoint date filter param (modifiedAfter / since / updatedSince) is present in any of the 15 OpenAPI specs. All record schemas carry sys_last_modified_at (ISO 8601 date-time, vendor-managed) and sys_created_at — these are server-side timestamps present on returned records. Incremental sync via the REST list endpoints would require a full scan + client-side timestamp filter. The System API provides a query execution engine for saved queries (POST /queries/{tenantId}/start/{queryType}) that could support server-side date filtering, but query definitions are tenant-specific and not declared in the connector. Recommended strategy: content-hash / sys_version change detection, or full-scan with client-side sys_last_modified_at comparison.
IncrementalSyncCapability.watermarkFieldNotes: sys_last_modified_at is present on all record schemas across all 15 modules and is the only server-managed modification timestamp. It can be used as a client-side watermark for post-fetch filtering, but NOT as a server-side filter param.

WebhooksAvailable.notes: Rhythm publishes real-time push events via AWS EventBridge (docs.api.rhythmsoftware.com/event-streams/eventbridge.md). This is a separate integration path from REST polling and is OUT OF SCOPE for the REST connector. EventBridge subscriptions are tenant-configured. A Zapier integration is also available as a separate path.

BulkOperationsAvailable.notes: Every module resource exposes POST /{resource}/{tenantId}/batch accepting up to 100 parallel patch/delete operations. Response: { error_count, results, success_count }. Batch supports "patch" and "delete" ops (per BatchOperationRequest schema). Create is not part of the batch envelope (individual POST for create).

WriteCapability.notes: All 15 modules expose full CRUD (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) on their primary resources. PATCH conforms to RFC 6902 JSON Patch (array of { op, path, value } directives). PUT replaces the full record. POST creates a new record (ID is auto-generated by Rhythm; specifying an ID on create throws an error). DELETE permanently removes the record (hard delete). Batch endpoint (POST /batch) supports patch and delete operations up to 100 at a time.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNotes: Every record carries sys_version (number) — a server-managed version counter incremented on each write. The OpenAPI specs do not show an If-Match or ETag header on PATCH/PUT requests; the version field is present in the record body but no optimistic-lock header protocol is documented. Conflict resolution is snapshot-3-way by default. sys_version can be used for change detection in the connector.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNotes: DELETE endpoints return HTTP 200 with a string (deleted record ID). No soft-delete tombstone flag on the record. The contact status enum includes "inactive" and "duplicate" values for logical status changes, but DELETE is a true hard delete. The sys_deleted_by_id field (read-only) records who performed the deletion, but deleted records are not retrievable via normal list endpoints.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNotes: No If-Match / ETag header protocol is documented in the specs (sys_version is in the body, not a concurrency-gated write header). MostRecent is not recommended without a reliable server-side compare-and-swap. DestWins is safe for read-first Pull default. If bidirectional is enabled, sys_version can inform a manual conflict review.

universalPK.notes: The "id" field is the universal primary key across all 15 Rhythm modules. 427 path-template occurrences of {id} as the single-record lookup param. Present in 414+ coverable record schemas with a description like "The unique, string identifier of this [entity]". Non-record schemas (Address, CustomFieldValue, SearchParameters) do not carry id but are not independent syncable resources. A small set of singleton-style config objects (ShippingConfiguration, TaxConfiguration) also lack id but are accessed via a fixed path without a record-level PK.

ErrorResponseShape.notes: Error responses (400/401/403/404/409/429/500) return no structured body in the OpenAPI specs — only an HTTP status code and a plain-text description. No JSON error envelope is declared in any of the 15 specs. 409 means the record refers to/depends on a non-existent object (on create) or other records depend on this one (on delete). 429 indicates tenant rate/limit exceeded.

statusCodes.400: Invalid request / validation error (no body schema)
statusCodes.429: Tenant limit exceeded (M2M token budget or tenant-configured request limit)

Configuration.CustomObjectNotes: Rhythm has a Platform module with CustomObject and CustomField endpoints that allow tenants to define custom objects and fields. These are tenant-specific and runtime-Discovered (not Declared). Each module record schema includes a custom_field_values array property (type CustomFieldValue) which holds tenant-specific custom field values. Custom field definitions (names, types) are accessed at runtime via GET /customFields/{tenantId} on the platform subdomain. No static pattern or prefix is used for custom objects/fields — they are identified by their Platform-module IDs.
Configuration.OutOfScopeFamiliesReason: tenant-specific / route-not-confirmed — deferred to runtime discovery per Rhythm no-invention policy; public REST API catalog is the in-scope contract-tier subset. The broader multi-route nature (Event Streams via AWS EventBridge, Zapier, SSO, WordPress, Sitefinity integration guides, tenant custom field schemas, tenant saved query IDs) and tenant-configured extensions are documented here as known gaps, not silently-unknown, so a future build can expand without re-discovering.
Configuration.TenantPathParamNotes: Every endpoint in all 15 modules requires {tenantId} as a path parameter (e.g. GET /contacts/{tenantId}, POST /contacts/{tenantId}). The tenantId is the Rhythm tenant identifier obtained at connection setup. It is distinct from the OAuth client credentials and must be stored as a separate credential or configuration field.
Configuration.OpenAPISpecNotes: 15 publicly accessible OpenAPI 3.x YAML specs, one per module. Version v1-2025-04-18. All reachable without authentication.
